US-119-HR4598.title: Technical Corrections to the Northwestern New Mexico Rural Water Projects Act, Taos Pueblo Indian Water Rights Settlement Act, and Aamodt Litigation Settlement Act
US-119-HR4598.summary:
Technical Corrections to the Northwestern New Mexico Rural Water Projects Act, Taos Pueblo Indian Water Rights Settlement Act, and Aamodt Litigation Settlement Act

This bill authorizes deposits representing unpaid interest into the Navajo Nation Water Resources Development Trust Fund, the Taos Pueblo Water Development Fund, and the Aamodt Settlement Pueblos’ Fund. These funds were established in 2009 and 2010 under certain water rights settlement agreements that did not allow accrual of interest.

These funds are tied to water rights settlement deals for Native communities in New Mexico. It would make technical fixes to those older laws.

US-119-HR10933.title: EMS SUPPORT Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

The money could help hire and support EMS staff, pay for training and required certificates, buy gear and supplies, and upgrade equipment, buildings, and vehicles. US-119-HR10911.description: To amend the Animal Health Protection Act to establish a U.S. Swine health improvement plan as a voluntary program to be administered by the Secretary of Agriculture in cooperation with the States and the swine industry to prevent the introduction into the United States of, and to monitor for, diseases that threaten swine health, and for other purposes.

It would certify certain pig facilities that meet rules for disease safety, tracking, and monitoring for diseases like African swine fever and classical swine fever. It would also require the final rule to be finished within 1 year after enactment and would authorize $4.5 million each year from fiscal 2027 through 2031.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

It would investigate alleged abuses of public office and other misconduct by U.S. officers and employees since January 20, 2025, and could also look at related private people and companies. The commission would make its findings public and could refer possible lawbreaking to federal or state authorities.

US-119-HR10713.title: Federal Telework Protection Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10713.description: To amend title 5, United States Code, to establish a process for considering telework requests of Federal employees, and for other purposes.

It would also require agencies to update and post their telework rules and would block federal funds from being used to carry out a 2025 order or directive that would end remote work and require in-person work.

US-119-S5673.title: Car Privacy Rights Act of 2026

It would require clear privacy notices, let people see certain data about them, and bar sharing or selling precise location data and most other car data without clear consent. It would also require companies to report their data practices to the Federal Trade Commission, which would then report to Congress and publish a summary.

US-119-S5651.aiSummary: The bill would create the National Institutes of Clean Energy as a new agency in the Department of Energy by January 1, 2030. It would fund clean energy and climate research, including projects on microgrids, energy storage, electric vehicles, and other advanced energy work, with priority for public colleges, land-grant schools, minority-serving schools, and areas with heavy job losses. US-119-S5552.title: Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act
US-119-S5552.summary:
Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act

This bill establishes a federal business tax credit for a percentage of the compensation paid for services performed in the United States related to a qualified film or television production. (Conditions and exceptions apply.)

The bill defines a qualified film or television production as any production that is
• a feature film, television pilot, or television season;
• produced in the ordinary course of business for commercial purposes;
• capitalized;
• completed during the tax year with more than $1 million in total costs; and
• filmed in the United States for 75% of the photography days.

Under the bill, various types of programming are not a qualified film or television production, including news programs, live sporting events, and programming intended primarily for social media platforms.

The amount of the tax credit is 20% (base tax credit percentage) of the compensation paid for services performed in the United States related to a qualified film or television production. The base tax credit percentage increases by increments of 5% (up to a maximum tax credit percentage of 30%) if
• at least 30% of the production is filmed in a federally declared disaster area or rural qualified opportunity zone,
• the production is independently produced, or
• the production meets certain multi-state or increased domestic production requirements.

Special rules apply to animations, visual effects productions, and post-production activities.

Finally, the tax credit may be transferred to an unrelated third party in exchange for cash.
US-119-S5552.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-09-24)

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5552.aiSummary: The bill would create a federal business tax credit for part of the pay for services tied to certain film and TV productions made in the United States. It would apply to qualified feature films, TV pilots, and TV seasons that meet set cost and filming rules, and it would not cover some shows like news, live sports, or content made mainly for social media. The credit would start at 20% and could rise to 30% if certain added conditions are met. The credit could also be sold to an unrelated buyer for cash.

US-119-S5475.title: Timely Access to Coverage Decisions Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5475.description: A bill to amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure timely review of local coverage determination requests under the Medicare program.
US-119-S5475.aiSummary: The bill would set deadlines for Medicare contractors to review requests for local coverage decisions and reconsideration requests. It would require them to say within 60 days whether a request is complete, and to act on complete requests within 1 year. It would also add public posting, comment, and meeting steps for some coverage decisions, and let interested parties ask the Secretary of Health and Human Services to review a contractor’s final decision.

US-119-HR6633.title: High-Capacity Grid Act
US-119-HR6633.summary:
High-Capacity Grid Act

This bill requires public electric utilities to use the best-available transmission conductor for certain interstate transmission lines (i.e., power lines) in order to recover the costs of the conductor through consumers' electric bills.

Specifically, in any filing seeking to recover the costs of a transmission conductor for the transmission line and in any proceeding to determine if the costs may be recovered through rates, the bill directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to presume that (1) the use of a best-available transmission conductor is a prudent practice and that the associated costs are just and reasonable, and (2) the use of a transmission conductor that is not a best-available transmission conductor is not prudent and that the associated costs are not just and reasonable.

A best-available transmission conductor is a conductor that (1) provides the greatest feasible and commercially available energy-carrying capacity at a given voltage level, (2) provides the highest feasible and commercially available electrical efficiency at that voltage level, and (3) mitigates thermal sag (drooping of power lines) at the maximum rated transmission-carrying capacity of the facility.

The bill applies to projects to (1) construct new transmission facilities; or (2) modify, upgrade, or replace an existing transmission line.

US-119-HR10438.title: SYLLABLE Act of 2026
US-119-HR10438.summary:

US-119-HR9548.title: Blair Holt Firearm Owner Licensing and Record of Sale Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9548.description: To provide for the implementation of a system of licensing for purchasers of certain firearms and for a record of sale system for those firearms, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9548.aiSummary: The bill would set up a federal license for people who buy or keep certain firearms, including handguns and some semiautomatic rifles. US-119-S4661.title: Ensuring Disaster Recovery and Resilience for Specialty Crops Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4661.description: A bill to amend the Federal Agriculture Improvement and Reform Act of 1996 to provide permanent disaster assistance for specialty crops, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4661.aiSummary: This bill would create a permanent aid program for growers of specialty crops, like fruits, vegetables, and nuts, when their crops are hurt by an adverse event, including an economic crisis or market disruption. The U.S. Agriculture Secretary would set the program rules and calculate payments based on past specialty crop sales and a payment factor for losses. It would also set payment limits, and some farming-based businesses could receive at least $500,000 as a maximum amount.
